HOW: rename the method to `def include_website_name?` (matching the framework convention used by the other predicates) so AMS actually honors the `website.present?` check.

issues.descricao: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

comentarios.texto: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.

Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. With an instance hostname of example.com and a valid website of http://EXAMPLE.COM/user, neither the exact-host nor suffix comparison matches, so the profile displays only EXAMPLE.COM instead of the requested path. Normalize both hostnames to lowercase for comparison while preserving the desired display spelling.

issues.descricao: website_name strips only the first label to decide same-domain, so unrelated hosts under multi-label public suffixes (co.uk, github.io) are treated as the instance domain and shown with full path.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `elsif` branch treats the last two dot-segments as the registrable domain, so multi-part public suffixes are mis-compared. WHY: for e.g. website_host='example.co.uk' and discourse_host='forum.co.uk' both have 3 segments, the branch compares `'co.uk' == 'co.uk'`, concludes the domains match, and returns `website_host + path`, even though example.co.uk and forum.co.uk are unrelated sites — the display then shows a path that does not belong to the instance domain, defeating the feature's purpose. HOW: compare against a public-suffix-aware registrable domain (e.g. use the PublicSuffix list) or require at least the full suffix before treating hosts as the same domain, instead of blindly taking `split('.')[1..-1]`.

Comparing all labels except the first incorrectly treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, with instance host `forum.co.uk` and website `https://unrelated.co.uk/user`, this returns `unrelated.co.uk/user` rather than the unrelated-site host-only label. Both hosts have three labels and their suffixes are `co.uk`, so this branch mistakes the public suffix for a shared site domain. Use registrable-domain-aware comparison (or a narrower explicit host relationship) before including the path.

The same-label-count branch treats two hosts as the same domain when everything after the first label matches. Unrelated hosts on shared suffixes, such as `a.github.io` and `b.github.io`, are treated as the same domain, so the full path is shown for an unrelated website. Compare against the registrable domain, for example with the PublicSuffix gem, or drop this heuristic branch.

issues.descricao: Claims website_name should also show the full path when the website is a subdomain of the instance host.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Else branch only tests `discourse_host.ends_with?('.'+website_host)` (discourse child of website) and misses the reverse (website subdomain of instance). WHY: With instance `example.com` and website `http://sub.example.com/page`, it returns `sub.example.com` instead of `sub.example.com/page`, contradicting the PR intent to show the full path for same-base-domain URLs. HOW: Also return host+path when `website_host` ends with `.`+discourse_host or shares the same registrable domain.

issues.descricao: website_name is not marked untrusted, so the host/path of a TL0 user's website, which is hidden from anonymous viewers, is still exposed through the new field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: website_name re-exposes the user's website for profiles where it is intentionally hidden — the attribute is added to the public `attributes` list (line 43) but not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` instead of `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. WHY: `website` is an untrusted attribute gated by `restrict_user_fields?` (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60), which is true for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor; `website_name` derives `website_host + path` from the same `object.user_profile.website`, so the URL that `include_website?` suppresses is still disclosed through the new key (the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-14 only asserts the listed untrusted keys are absent, so this leak is not covered). HOW: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or have `include_website_name` return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), mirroring the `website` handling.

`website_name` is derived from the same `object.user_profile.website` value that `:website` protects via `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), but it is only gated by `include_website_name` -> `website.present?`. Since the untrusted filter removes `website` for some viewers while `website_name` is still emitted, and in the same-domain / subdomain branches it returns host *plus* `URI(website).path` (lines 143/146/149), the user's full website URL still leaves in the response for viewers the filter was supposed to strip it from. Either add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate `include_website_name` with the same trust condition as `website`.

The new `website_name` field is gated only on `website.present?`, ignoring the visibility constraint this file declares for its source attribute: lines 105-111 put `:website` in `untrusted_attributes`, so `website` is omitted for viewers not allowed to see profile fields, but `website_name` is still serialized because `include_website_name` never consults that condition. Those viewers now receive the user's URL host, and when the host equals (lines 141-143) or is a parent of (144-149) the instance host they receive host + path, i.e. the complete URL that `website` was supposed to hide. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (105-111) — or make the guard reuse `website`'s own inclusion condition instead of a bare presence check.

issues.descricao: include_website_name lacks the '?' suffix that ActiveModelSerializers requires, so the conditional-inclusion guard is never called.
issues.textoGolden: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` required by ActiveModelSerializers. WHY: every other conditional-inclusion guard in this file uses the `?` form (`define_method "include_#{attr}?"` at lines 9/18/27, `include_email?` at line 117), and AMS 0.8.3 resolves the guard as `include_<attr>?`; because this method lacks the `?` it is never invoked, so the intended `website.present?` condition is silently ignored and `website_name` is always serialized. HOW: rename to `def include_website_name?`.

The guard method is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers (and this file's own convention, e.g. `include_email?` at line 117) resolves per-attribute guards via `include_<attribute>?`. Because the name lacks the trailing `?`, the framework never invokes it: the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting `website_name: null` for users without a website. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

The conditional-inclusion guard is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers resolves these guards as `include_<attribute>?` (the sibling in this very file is `include_email?` at line 117). As written the method is never called, so the guard is dead and the `:website_name` attribute declared at line 43 is serialized unconditionally. That defeats the intent of the guard (`website.present?`): the payload now always carries `website_name`, including for the scopes where `website` itself is withheld by the `untrusted_attributes` list (line 109), leaking the user's site host/path to viewers who were never meant to receive the website. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` so the serializer base class honors it.

issues.descricao: UserSerializer#website_name re-parses URI(website.to_s) for the path after already parsing it for the host instead of reusing one parsed URI.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time on grantType instead of validating rawTokenId. WHY: rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null raw id is silently accepted and encodeTokenId then produces a corrupt id ending in ':null' (and the error message is misleading). HOW: change line 73 to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");

WHAT: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) and then returns false when it equals expectedGrantShortcut (the condition is inverted). WHY: the encoded id is '<session><token><grant>:<uuid>' so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6); the wrong offset never matches, and even if it did, the inverted equals means the matcher never enforces the grant shortcut, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken/device tests pass regardless of the actual grant type and provide no coverage of the new encoding. HOW: use items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) and return false when it does NOT equal (i.e. `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).
AccessTokenContext.requireNonNull copy-paste defect at line 73.
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId has inverted equals and substring(3,5) vs (4,6).

issues.descricao: The AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and is encoded as ':null'.
issues.textoGolden: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the constructor validates `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`). WHY: a null `rawTokenId` is silently accepted, so `encodeTokenId` produces a token id ending in `:null` and any later consumer of the raw id gets an invalid value instead of an early failure. HOW: change the argument to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

Line 73 calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — it validates grantType a second time (line 72 already does) with a message naming a different field. rawTokenId is never validated, so a null rawTokenId is accepted at construction and the advertised check/message is wrong. It should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

The null-check message names the wrong parameter: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` validates `grantType` but reports `rawTokenId`, and it duplicates the check on line 72 while `rawTokenId` is never validated at all. The message that reaches the reader contradicts the code it guards; it should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

issues.descricao: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset (3,5 instead of 4,6) and inverts the comparison, so the event assertions never verify the token's grant type.
issues.textoGolden: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `isAccessTokenId` reads the grant shortcut from the wrong offset and inverts the comparison — `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. WHY: for the encoded id `ssttgg:raw` the grant shortcut occupies 0-based indices 4-5, so `substring(3,5)` inspects the token-type/grant boundary and can never equal the expected shortcut; combined with the inverted `return false`, the equality branch is unreachable and the matcher validates only the UUID part. As a result the new assertions in `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` do not actually assert the grant type and would pass even if the grant shortcut were wrong. HOW: use `items[0].substring(4, 6)` and negate the condition (`if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).

The matcher logic is inverted: line 483 returns false when the extracted grant shortcut EQUALS expectedGrantShortcut, so a token that actually carries the expected grant fails the matcher, while a token with any other grant shortcut falls through and passes. The condition should be negated: `if (!items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also note the encode site writes the grant shortcut at chars 4-6 (substring(4,6)); substring(3,5) reads one character early into the token-type field, so the offset is off by one relative to TokenManager.encodeTokenId.

The comment 'Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char' disagrees with the encoding that this PR defines (sessionType chars 1-2, tokenType 3-4, grantType 5-6, e.g. 'trltcc'), and the code reads substring(3,5) — the 4th-5th chars, i.e. the token-type second char plus the grant first char, never the grant shortcut. The comment (and the index) should point at the 5th char / substring(4,6).

issues.descricao: getShortcut() Javadoc says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, but the encoding requires exactly 2-character shortcuts.
issues.textoGolden: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc says getShortcut() returns 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but every implementation introduced in this PR returns a 2-character shortcut ('ac','cc','pg','pc','rt','ro','te','ci','dg') and the encoder relies on exactly 2 chars (encoded context length 6 = 2+2+2). The doc states a length the code does not produce; it should say 2-character shortcut.

Grant shortcuts are registered without enforcing the two-character length required by the decoder. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut, which the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation explicitly suggests, produces a seven-character prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects, breaking encode/decode round trips for that grant. Validate shortcut length during registration and dynamic refresh, and document the required two-character format.

The new contract describes getShortcut() as usually returning a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires exactly two characters for the grant field (six total prefix characters, decoded with substring(4, 6)). An extension author following this documentation can produce token IDs that the default decoder rejects. Document the required two-character length rather than advertising three letters.

issues.descricao: testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, so it passes on a NullPointerException from the unset sessionFactory rather than verifying the unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException.
issues.textoGolden: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

comentarios.texto: Catching RuntimeException allows this negative test to pass for an unrelated fixture failure. The fixture constructs the factory without postInit, leaving sessionFactory null; resolving the unregistered `ac` shortcut calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream and throws NullPointerException before the decoder's intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException. Catch/assert IllegalArgumentException specifically and provide a factory fixture whose lookup returns no matching grant, so removing the decoder's validation would fail the test.

issues.descricao: Client-credentials (and UMA permission) token issuance never sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their access token ids are encoded with the unknown grant 'na' instead of their shortcut.

comentarios.texto: The new grant metadata falls back to 'na' for client-credentials and UMA tokens because their issuance paths never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on their fresh ClientSessionContext. ClientCredentialsGrantType calls responseBuilder.generateAccessToken directly, and PermissionGrantType delegates to AuthorizationTokenService, so neither executes the new assignment in createTokenResponse; tokens from these known grants therefore carry unknown grant context. Set the grant attribute in both issuance paths before generating the access token.

issues.descricao: Lazy registration of newly deployed grants does not check shortcut uniqueness, so a grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and older tokens decode to the wrong grant.

comentarios.texto: Enforce shortcut uniqueness during lazy registration rather than overwriting grantsByShortcuts. If a newly deployed grant B uses existing grant A's shortcut, this path replaces shortcut→A with shortcut→B while retaining both forward entries. Previously issued A tokens then decode as B. Concurrent registrations of two new grants with the same shortcut likewise both succeed, with the last inverse-map write winning. Use collision-aware atomic registration and reject the conflicting grant before publishing its forward mapping.

issues.descricao: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default, breaking existing custom grant type factories (compile error or AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it).

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The eviction `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` drops spans purely by lowest end_timestamp_precise and never exempts the segment/root span. WHY: When a segment accumulates more than 1000 spans, a root span (notably an is_remote segment span, or any span whose end_timestamp_precise is earlier than its children due to clock skew) is evicted from the sorted set, so done_flush_segments ships a segment with no root/segment span, breaking downstream segment reconstruction. HOW: Before calling zpopmin, compute the segment span member (the payload whose span_id == set_span_id) and re-insert/exclude it (e.g. ZRANGEBYSCORE for `span_count - 1000` victims, remove all but the segment span, and ZADD the retained segment span back) so the root is always preserved.

WHAT: The flush-time `max_segment_spans` overflow guard was deleted (the `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ... del payloads[key]; del cursors[key]` block), yet the constructor still accepts/stores `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and it is now referenced nowhere. WHY: Any deployment that configured `max_segment_spans` to a custom value is silently ignored — the effective cap is now hardcoded to 1000 inside add-buffer.lua — so the configured contract no longer holds and oversized-segment protection can no longer be tuned. HOW: Thread the span-count limit into the Lua script/config (or remove the now-dead `max_segment_spans` field) and keep a consistent value between buffer.py and the eviction threshold in add-buffer.lua.

WHAT: `p.zscan(key, ...)` (and the Lua `zcard`/`zunionstore`) now read segment keys `span-buf:s:*` that were created as plain Redis SETs by the previous code. WHY: During rollout, in-flight segment keys created before this change remain set-typed for up to redis_ttl (3600s); ZSCAN/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE against a set returns a WRONGTYPE ResponseError, aborting the pipeline/batch and dropping spans until those keys expire. HOW: Version the key prefix (e.g. `span-buf:z:*`) so old set keys and new zset keys never collide, or flush/ignore old set-typed keys during deploy before issuing sorted-set commands.

issues.descricao: ZUNIONSTORE merges sorted sets with the default SUM aggregate, so a span payload present in both keys gets a doubled end-timestamp score and is wrongly kept by the oldest-first eviction.

comentarios.texto: ZUNIONSTORE uses AGGREGATE SUM by default, so when the same span payload is present in both `set_key` and the merged `span_key`/`parent_key` (duplicate delivery is anticipated by this buffer's own comments), its score is added instead of being kept equal to `end_timestamp_precise`. Because eviction at line 63 (`zpopmin` by score) compares scores across all members of `set_key`, a summed score makes the duplicated span appear far newer than its real end timestamp and biases eviction away from legitimately-old spans, breaking the stated 'evict oldest end timestamps' contract. Use ZUNIONSTORE ... AGGREGATE MIN (or MAX) so a duplicate keeps a single end timestamp score rather than doubling it.

ZUNIONSTORE uses its default SUM aggregation, so replayed payloads present in both the temporary parent_key and the resolved set_key receive the sum of their end timestamps. Replaying a child whose parent already redirects to an ancestor therefore makes that old span score roughly twice its actual timestamp, protecting it from eviction over genuinely newer spans. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN for identical timestamp scores) on both union operations to preserve timestamp scores when members overlap.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, so a payload present in both the destination and source has its timestamp doubled rather than preserved. This can happen when a previously merged span is replayed into its original subtree key. The duplicated span then sorts after genuinely newer spans and survives ZPOPMIN eviction incorrectly. Specify AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN, since identical payloads should have identical timestamps) on both union calls so merging remains idempotent and scores remain end timestamps.

issues.descricao: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under the same key names, so keys left by the previous release make ZADD, ZCARD and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, crashing span processing and flushing.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Changed SET ops (scard/sunionstore) to ZSET ops (zcard/zunionstore/zpopmin) with no migration breaks in-flight segments. WHY: Old keys of type SET still live up to TTL; ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZADD on the opposite type raises WRONGTYPE and fails inserts/flushes during rollout.

The segment keys were migrated from Redis SETs to SORTED SETs (ZADD/ZSCAN/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN), but nothing handles the keys written by the currently deployed release. During a rolling deploy, an existing `span-buf:s:{...}:{id}` key is still a SET, so this `p.zadd(...)` (and the flusher's `p.zscan(...)`, and the Lua `zcard`/`zunionstore`) raises WRONGTYPE 'Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value'. That exception is unhandled: it aborts the whole pipeline/Lua invocation and crashes the consumer batch. Add a key-schema version to the key name (or a migration/fallback) so old SET-typed keys cannot be touched as sorted sets.

The new ZADD writes sorted sets into the same span-buf:s namespace previously populated by SADD, without migrating existing set keys. During deployment, inserting into an existing buffered segment fails with WRONGTYPE, and the new ZSCAN reader likewise fails on pending old-format segments instead of flushing them. Introduce a coordinated migration/drain or a versioned namespace with compatible handling of pending old-format buffers.

issues.descricao: Claims zpopmin eviction can drop the root span while the has-root flag stays set, flushing a segment without its root.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zpopmin eviction by lowest end_timestamp has no protection for the segment/root span. WHY: Root with smallest or tied timestamp (tests use identical timestamps, ties break lexicographically) is evicted while hrs flag stays 1, flushing a root-marked segment missing its root.

issues.descricao: max_segment_spans is still a constructor parameter but is no longer enforced; the segment cap is now hardcoded to 1000 in the Lua script, so the configured value is ignored.

comentarios.texto: This hunk removes the only load-time span-count cap (`self.max_segment_spans`): previously a segment exceeding 1001 spans was logged, deleted from `payloads`/`cursors`, and skipped, but now every scanned span is unconditionally appended via `payloads[key].extend(...)`. The new bound relies entirely on insert-time eviction in the Lua script; if that eviction fails to bound a key (e.g. duplicated/scored members or the concurrent-writer case the code itself warns about at lines 457-461), this method will now materialize an unbounded number of spans into memory and emit them, whereas before it was safely skipped. Re-introduce a span-count guard (or verify the invite-time eviction strictly caps cardinality) to keep memory bounded.

buffer.py declares the segment span limit as the configurable `max_segment_spans` (default 1001, line 150) and this hunk removed the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` size guard from the flush path, while the other changed file (add-buffer.lua line 62) now enforces a hardcoded cap of 1000 spans. The two changed files disagree on what the segment span limit is: the Lua cap (1000) is not the declared `max_segment_spans`, and the buffer no longer applies the declared limit at all. If `max_segment_spans` is configured below 1000 (or below the Lua cap), oversized segments that this code used to skip will now be flushed. Reconcile the constant: either keep/restore the buffer-side guard against `self.max_segment_spans`, or make the Lua cap derive from the same limit instead of hardcoding 1000.

The segment size cap is hardcoded as 1000 here, but SpansBuffer still declares max_segment_spans = 1001 in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py, and this PR deleted the flush-time guard that used that constant. The declared limit and the actually-enforced limit now disagree (and the Python constant is no longer honored anywhere). Make the Lua cap and the Python constant agree — either pass max_segment_spans in as an ARGV instead of the literal 1000, or update the declared constant to 1000 — so the buffer's enforced bound matches the value it declares.

issues.descricao: Tests give every span the same end timestamp and never exceed 1000 spans, so the new score ordering and oldest-first eviction are not tested.

comentarios.texto: All spans in the fixture use identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0, so the ZSET score-dependent behavior (ordering by end time, zunionstore score merge, and Lua zpopmin keeping newest 1000) is neutralised — tests pass even if scores are wrong or eviction keeps the wrong end. Use distinct timestamps and add a >1000-span trimming test asserting oldest evicted.
The missing test for the new trim path (zset ordering/trim by end_timestamp_precise, the >1000-span zpopmin path) is a coverage gap. Add a test that verifies the new trim behavior.

issues.descricao: The span redirect-walk limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 iterations, so trees deeper than 1000 may not resolve to the correct segment root.
The spans buffer module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as plain sets, though they are now sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise and trimmed to 1000 spans by add-buffer.lua.
The set_key variable name no longer matches the sorted-set data type after the switch to zadd/zscan.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but defines only `pass`, leaving the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data unimplemented. WHY: ABCMeta forbids instantiating a class with remaining abstract methods, so `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for any Detector whose type slug resolves to MetricAlertFire; previously this handler was instantiable, so this is a regression. HOW: implement the required abstract methods (or keep MetricAlertDetectorHandler deriving from a concrete base / provide the four overrides) so the class can be instantiated.

The expected IssueOccurrence is built with group_key "val1" (`build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`), but the assertion calls `handler.evaluate_group_key_value(expected_result.group_key, 10, ...)` where `expected_result.group_key == "group_key"`. Since `build_fingerprint` embeds the group_key and DetectorEvaluationResult/IssueOccurrence are frozen dataclasses with field-based equality, the handler produces a fingerprint `<id>:group_key` while the expected occurrence has `<id>:val1`, so the equality assertion fails. This test passed before the PR only because `result` was None (the occurrence hook did not exist); the new hook makes the mismatch observable. Fix by building the expected occurrence with `expected_result.group_key` (or setting the expected group_key to "val1") so both sides use the same group key.

issues.descricao: The TODO above MetricAlertDetectorHandler says it will become a stateful detector, but the class already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now stale. MetricAlertDetectorHandler already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler. Remove or reword the TODO.

Remove or revise the adjacent TODO saying this will become a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'. The class now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, so the comment describes already-completed work as a future migration and misleads maintainers about which abstraction this handler uses.

issues.descricao: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.
issues.textoGolden: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data declared on StatefulDetectorHandler. WHY: the class is now abstract, and Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) instantiates it via group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector whose type resolves to this grouptype will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler — the previous version implemented evaluate and was instantiable. HOW: implement the required abstract methods (or keep a concrete evaluate override) so the handler can be constructed.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but with `pass`, so it implements none of the abstract methods it inherits (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class is therefore still abstract and instantiating it (it is registered as `detector_handler` on MetricAlertFire and is constructed by Detector.detector_handler) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Before this change it subclassed DetectorHandler and implemented the single abstract `evaluate`, so it was instantiable; the PR makes the metric-alert handler path throw. Either implement the required abstract methods or keep the class free of unimplemented abstracts.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods — counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data (detector.py:142-170) — none of which are implemented here. The class therefore remains abstract and cannot be instantiated; Detector.detector_handler's `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for the metric_alert_fire group type. Previously this class was a concrete DetectorHandler with an implemented evaluate, so this PR newly makes it uninstantiable. Implement the required abstract methods (or revert to a concrete handler) to satisfy the base-class contract.

issues.descricao: The evaluate() docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but it now returns a dict keyed by group key.
issues.textoGolden: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

comentarios.texto: Update evaluate's adjacent docstring to describe a dictionary keyed by DetectorGroupKey rather than a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This change returns a dictionary and callers now consume .values(), but the documented return contract still tells readers to expect a list; iterating the documented result as a list would instead yield group keys.
Docstring says 'returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult' but signature/body now return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Update docstring to describe dict keyed by group_key.

The evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. The method now returns a dict mapping group key to `DetectorEvaluationResult`. Update the docstring to describe the dict return shape.

issues.descricao: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
issues.textoGolden: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

comentarios.texto: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value: int` parameter but never uses it — the returned IssueOccurrence is derived only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Because `value` is dead, callers can pass a mismatched value with no failure: in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `6`. Either use `value` when constructing the occurrence so the test validates the group value, or drop the unused parameter and pass the correct value; otherwise the test silently accepts wrong group values.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Moving the lock from the whole BuildIndex function to only the `b.cache[key] = idx` write removes the mutual exclusion around index construction, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now run simultaneously. WHY: BuildIndex is reachable concurrently for the same key (Search is a concurrent gRPC method calling getOrCreateIndex at search.go:148/160, and search.init builds keys in a parallel errgroup); both goroutines will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk directory (bleve.go:96-98 when size > FileThreshold), flush, and then overwrite the cache, so the index instance returned to one caller is silently discarded and its writes are lost, plus a concurrent open/flush of the same bleve directory can corrupt it. The pre-existing TODO in getOrCreateIndex ("we want to block while building the index and return the same index for the key") shows this hazard was previously masked by the global lock. HOW: keep a per-key in-flight guard (e.g. a `sync.Map` of mutexes keyed by NamespacedResource, or singleflight) around the build so only the first caller builds and the rest reuse the cached index, while leaving the lock on the cache map write.

The new `s.log.Info(..., "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` call reads the bleve cache map without synchronizing with a concurrent writer. WHAT: `TotalDocs()` (bleve.go:144-154) iterates `b.cache` with no `cacheMu` lock, and it is invoked one line after search.go:207-213 starts the event-handler goroutine whose `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `build` → `BuildIndex` path writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()`. WHY: this is an unsynchronized concurrent map read and write, which the Go runtime handles as a fatal `concurrent map read and map write` that cannot be recovered and crashes the process. HOW: have `TotalDocs` hold `b.cacheMu.RLock()` while ranging over the map (or lock around the call), so the read cannot overlap the locked write.

issues.descricao: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.
issues.textoGolden: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Removing the function-wide `b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()` and keeping only the lock around `b.cache[key]=idx` removes the only thing that serialized GetIndex against an in-flight build. WHY: getOrCreateIndex (resource/search.go:287-307) does GetIndex -> if nil -> build; previously BuildIndex held the write lock for its whole body so a concurrent caller's GetIndex (RLock) blocked until the first build cached the index and then saw it (no second build). Now GetIndex can return nil while a build for the same key is still running, so two requests/watch events build the SAME key concurrently — producing two distinct index instances where the caller holding the non-cached one never observes later writes (stale search results), and, for file-backed indices (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` opening the same on-disk directory. HOW: guard the build per key (e.g. re-check the cache under the write lock after acquiring it, or use a per-key single-flight/lock so only one build runs per NamespacedResource), rather than relying on a global write lock held for the entire body.

The cache mutex was moved to cover only the cache assignment, removing the serialization that previously surrounded the whole BuildIndex. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now both construct an index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk path) and both write `b.cache[key]`; the second overwrites the first, so callers get distinct index instances for one key and writes made through the losing instance are invisible to readers of the cached one (and the file-backed build may collide on the same directory). Keep the build for a given key serialized (e.g. restore the lock around the build, or take a per-key lock) instead of locking only the map write.

Locking only cache publication allows concurrent requests for the same uncached key to build separate indexes and overwrite each other's cache entries. Search and handleEvent both call getOrCreateIndex, whose GetIndex previously blocked behind the build-wide lock; now an event can update one newly built index before another build replaces it, losing that update from subsequent search results and leaving the discarded index open. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that per-key guard.

issues.descricao: The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
issues.textoGolden: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

comentarios.texto: The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call is unsafe: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-150) iterates `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`, while the bleve.go hunk in this same PR keeps `cacheMu` for the `b.cache[key] = idx` write only. Because search.go:207-213 already started the watch-event goroutine that can call `build` → `BuildIndex` → cache write, line 216 can iterate the map concurrently with that write, causing a `concurrent map iteration and map write` panic or data race. Either guard the `TotalDocs` read with `cacheMu`, or move this call to a point where no build can run concurrently.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs after launching the write-event listener, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu.RLock. A write event for an unindexed resource can concurrently publish an index through BuildIndex, causing a map iteration/write race and potentially a fatal runtime error during initialization. Protect TotalDocs cache iteration with the same read lock used by GetIndex.

BuildIndex now writes b.cache under Lock while TotalDocs (called from search.init after the watch goroutine starts) ranges over b.cache without any lock. This can cause a concurrent map read/write fatal error. Fix by taking cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

issues.descricao: NewResourceServer returns an error when Init fails without cancelling the server context created earlier.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and, on error, returns `nil, err` without invoking the `cancel` func created at line 229 and without running any lifecycle cleanup. WHY: Init may have already started long-lived goroutines — searchSupport.init's event-consumption loop uses context.Background() (resource/search.go:202) and initWatcher starts a watcher bound to s.ctx (server.go:752-770) — so if search.init succeeds and initWatcher (or a later step) fails, the constructor discards the server while those goroutines keep running with no way to stop them, leaking the internal context and watcher goroutines. HOW: on the error path call `cancel()` (and any needed lifecycle.Stop) before returning, or defer the cancel until success.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously but returns nil,err without calling the cancel created for s.ctx. WHY: Failed startup leaks the server context (and any lifecycle/watch resources partially started by Init), leaving goroutines/channel watches alive. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (and lifecycle Stop cleanup) before returning.

issues.descricao: The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

sugestoes.texto: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the delegate model is absent, violating the documented contract of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() ('Never returns null', server-spi/GroupModel.java:296). This null flows through GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount (GroupUtils.java:90) into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount and out to REST clients/admin-console code that treats subGroupCount as numeric (e.g. js GroupPickerDialog.tsx / Members.tsx), which can produce a null where a number is expected. Return a non-null sentinel (e.g. 0L) when model is null, or delegate the miss to a fresh lookup, instead of returning null.

The reader thread is non-daemon and is only stopped by deletedAll.set(true) at line 155; if any remove() in the groupUuuids.forEach loop throws (server/connection error), that line is skipped and the thread loops forever calling groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true), leaking a non-daemon thread that keeps hammering the server and can prevent the test/JVM from terminating. Set the thread to daemon and/or guard the loop with try/finally (or join the thread) so it always terminates even when the test body fails.

The test asserts on `caughtExceptions` immediately after `deletedAll.set(true)` without joining the reader thread, so a read that is still in flight when the deletions finish can append its exception after the assertion, letting the test pass even when the NPE regression it targets occurs (false negative). The reader thread is also left running (non-daemon, never joined), so it can continue issuing admin calls into subsequent tests. Fix: after setting `deletedAll` and before asserting, join the reader thread (e.g. store the Thread and call `thread.join(...)`), and make it a daemon thread so a failure in `remove()` cannot leak a spinning thread.

issues.descricao: The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: runSplitQuery now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), which runs addAdHocFilters, but the resulting sub-requests still go through datasource.runQuery → DataSourceWithBackend.query, which applies applyTemplateVariables (and thus addAdHocFilters) a second time. WHY: addAdHocFilters is not idempotent for parsed/structured-metadata labels (addFilterAsLabelFilter in modifyQuery.ts:511 appends `| key=op\`value\`` with no dedup; only the indexed-label branch dedups), so adhoc label filters are appended twice (three times in the shard path: runShardSplitQuery at shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 + runSplitQuery + backend), producing duplicated `| key=...` label filters that can change results or fail LogQL validation. HOW: either pass the already-interpolated targets through without re-applying interpolation in runSplitQuery (e.g. interpolate once at the entry point and let downstream skip it), or make addAdHocFilters idempotent (dedup in addFilterAsLabelFilter like addFilterToStreamSelector does).

WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, and the resulting targets are then re-interpolated by the delegated `runSplitQuery` (querySplitting.ts:299) and again by `runQuery → DataSourceWithBackend.query` (DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185), so `applyTemplateVariables` — and thus `addAdHocFilters` — runs 2–3 times on the same query. WHY: the parsed/structured-metadata branch `addFilterAsLabelFilter` (modifyQuery.ts:511) has no dedup (unlike `addFilterToStreamSelector`, which uses `labelExists`), so an ad-hoc filter on a parsed label is appended once per pass, producing duplicated pipeline filters like `count_over_time({a="b"} | logfmt | level=`error` | level=`error`[5m])`, changing the query the backend executes versus the single-pass path at datasource.ts:343. HOW: interpolate the targets exactly once up front and prevent re-interpolation downstream (e.g. mark the already-interpolated queries so `runSplitQuery`/`DataSourceWithBackend.query` skip them, or make `applyTemplateVariables`/`addAdHocFilters` idempotent by checking for the existing label filter before appending).

issues.descricao: Loki split/shard queries are now interpolated with applyTemplateVariables before splitting and again on execution, so ad hoc filters are applied twice and already-substituted values are re-interpolated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 52), but it then delegates each sub-request to runSplitQuery (line 163), which this PR also changed to call datasource.applyTemplateVariables again (querySplitting.ts:299), so each target is interpolated (and ad hoc filters applied) twice. WHY: double interpolation re-runs addAdHocFilters on an already-filtered expression; the stream-selector path masks the duplicate via labelExists() dedup in addFilterToStreamSelector (modifyQuery.ts:494), but parsed/structured-metadata labels use addFilterAsLabelFilter which does not dedup, producing duplicated label filters, and any interpolated value containing '$' can be re-interpolated. This is confirmed by the updated test expecting applyTemplateVariables toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) for a single target (1 call here + 4 sub-requests through runSplitQuery) instead of 1. HOW: interpolate only once — either remove the interpolation added to runShardSplitQuery and let runSplitQuery do it, or have splitQueriesByStreamShard pass the already-interpolated targets without re-interpolating in runSplitQuery.

The newly interpolated targets are interpolated again by DataSourceWithBackend.query when runQuery executes each split request. TemplateSrv.replace scans the resulting string again, so a variable whose literal value contains another defined variable token (for example, a log-search value containing `$other`) is expanded a second time and produces a different query from the non-splitting path; shard splitting also passes through this additional interpolation. Preserve the early interpolation needed for partitioning while ensuring already-interpolated targets are not interpolated again on execution, and test through the real backend query preparation rather than mocking runQuery.

Targets are interpolated here with `applyTemplateVariables`, including ad hoc filters, and then sent to `datasource.runQuery`, which interpolates them again through the backend path (datasource.ts:324/377). The ad hoc filters may be injected twice, and already-substituted values are re-interpolated, which can produce wrong or invalid LogQL. Interpolate only once. Either clear `scopedVars` and `filters` on the sub-requests after the first pass, or skip interpolation in `runQuery` for already-interpolated requests. The same issue applies to shardQuerySplitting.ts:52.

issues.descricao: runShardSplitQuery now filters empty/hidden targets before interpolation, so an expr that interpolates to an empty string is no longer dropped.

comentarios.texto: The order of operations was inverted relative to the previous contract: interpolation used to run before the `expr`/`hide` filters (interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets).filter(...)), and now the filters run on the *raw* targets before `applyTemplateVariables` is applied. Filtering on the un-interpolated `query.expr` means the previous fallback that dropped a target once variable substitution had emptied its expression no longer exists: a target like `{ expr: '$myVar' }` whose variable resolves to '' is truthy at filter time, survives, is then interpolated to `''`, and is passed into the shard splitting/execution loop as a blank query. To preserve the old contract the filters should run on the interpolated result (or the interpolated expr should be re-checked for emptiness).

sugestoes.texto: Adding @include flexbox() to .small-action turns its .small-action-desc child into a shrink-to-fit flex item instead of the full-width block it was before. The edit/delete buttons inside .small-action-desc (styled `button { float: right }` at lines 306-310) and the avatar float are positioned relative to the desc's block width; with the desc no longer stretching across the 755px row (desktop/topic-post.scss:730), these floated controls no longer align to the right edge and the desc's width collapses to its content. Give .small-action-desc `flex: 1` (or `flex-grow: 1`) so it keeps filling the row, matching how .panel was handled with margin-left:auto in header.scss.

Making `.d-header .contents` a flex container turns `.extra-info-wrapper` into a flex item, and it has no `flex`/`min-width` set. WHY: previously `.extra-info-wrapper` was a full-width block so its child `.topic-link { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }` (desktop/topic-post.scss:532) truncated long topic titles; as a flex item with the default `min-width: auto`, its min-content size equals the full unbreakable title, so it cannot shrink and long titles no longer truncate (they overflow/clip the header). HOW: give `.extra-info-wrapper` (`@include order(2)` in common/base/topic.scss:30) `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;` so it can shrink and the ellipsis works again.

issues.descricao: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.

comentarios.texto: The flex-item styling targets the inner .extra-info-wrapper rather than the outer div generated by header-extra-info's Ember.Component. With .contents now using flexbox, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so a long nowrap topic title cannot shrink to the available space and pushes the navigation panel outside the header instead of being ellipsized by the existing desktop truncation rules. Move the extra-info-wrapper class onto the component's root element and set min-width: 0 on that flex item so ordering and truncation apply to the actual header child.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

comentarios.texto: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which never existed in IE/Edge; the legacy property is -ms-flex-align, so the declaration is dead.
issues.textoGolden: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: align-items() mixin emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is not a valid IE10/11 property (only -ms-flex-align exists). WHY: dead declaration shows wrong contract and leaves IE alignment dependent solely on -ms-flex-align, which also breaks for flex-start/flex-end values. HOW: remove the -ms-align-items line and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align.

issues.descricao: Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.
issues.textoGolden: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

issues.descricao: After .small-action becomes a flex container, float: left on .topic-avatar is dead CSS.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` is called before `.compact`, so a nil `default_locale` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil`. WHY: `SiteSetting.default_locale` can be nil (the codebase guards for this at db.rake:3/28 and jobs/base.rb:151), and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` runs on every request via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `set_locale`, so a nil value crashes all requests instead of degrading. HOW: symbolize defensively after the nil filter, e.g. `.compact.map(&:to_sym).uniq` or `(SiteSetting.default_locale || :en).to_sym`, so nils are removed before conversion.

WHAT: `ensure_loaded!` reads the shared `@loaded_locales` array (`||= []` and `.include?`) without acquiring `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array (`<<`) under that mutex from other threads. WHY: concurrent translation requests can read the array during another thread's mutation (unsynchronized read/write on shared state), and the pre-check is redundant since `load_locale` already re-checks under the lock. HOW: drop the outer check and let `load_locale` handle the guard, and initialize the array safely under the mutex (e.g. `load_locale(locale)`; move `@loaded_locales ||= []` inside the synchronized block or into `reload!`).

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new CAUTION block tells users the Keycloak Operator will fail unless the preview feature `rolling-updates` is enabled, but no operator code enforces that feature. WHY: Grepping operator/src/main for ROLLING_UPDATES / isFeatureEnabled / Profile.Feature finds nothing — the only FeatureSpec usage is KeycloakDistConfigurator mapping `features` to the Keycloak container config, and UpgradeLogicFactory/UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy never read the feature — so the documented failure can never occur and users who omit the feature get no error, contradicting the caution (and the UpgradeTest had to enable the feature even though the operator does not require it). HOW: Add an explicit check in the operator upgrade path (e.g. in UpgradeLogicFactory/KeycloakController) that rejects the rolling strategy when the feature is disabled, or correct the documentation so it matches actual behavior.

WHAT: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 (its former value is reused for the new FEATURE_DISABLED code). WHY: The update-compatibility guide explicitly instructs users to build automation around the command's exit code, so any existing script that keys off exit code 4 to mean 'recreate upgrade required' will now see 3 and misinterpret the result (or miss that the feature is disabled and get 4). This is a silent break of a documented scriptable contract. HOW: Preserve backward compatibility by keeping the recreate code stable and allocating FEATURE_DISABLED a previously-unused value, or version/announce the exit-code change explicitly rather than silently renumbering.

issues.descricao: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand, so the feature guard in the check subcommand is untested.

comentarios.texto: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the `metadata` subcommand and never the `check` subcommand. Removing the feature guard from UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() would therefore not fail any test. It also doesn't assert the exit code (FEATURE_DISABLED=4). Add a case for `check` and assert the exit code on both.

WHAT: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand disabled path and never the check subcommand. WHY: the feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run can be removed or broken without failing any test since no assertion covers its disabled message/exit code. HOW: also launch/assert the check command without --features (e.g. parameterize over metadata and check subcommands or add a second Launch).

testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand, leaving the identical ROLLING_UPDATES gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck unverified. If the Check gate were removed, the suite still passes. Parameterize/add a second @Launch for {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME} (with required --file or not) asserting the disabled message and FEATURE_DISABLED exit code.

issues.descricao: The disabled-feature test checks only the error message, not that the command exits with FEATURE_DISABLED (4).

comentarios.texto: The new disabled-feature test only verifies the error text, not the failure exit status. If the metadata command still prints this diagnostic but exits with 0 (or another incorrect code) instead of FEATURE_DISABLED (4), this test would still pass. Assert that cliResult.exitCode() equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED so the test actually protects the new disabled-feature failure contract.

issues.descricao: testMissingOptionOnSave only asserts a message is absent, so it would still pass if --features=rolling-updates were not honoured and the command failed with the feature-disabled error.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: instrumentPluginRequest (and instrumentPluginRequestSize at lines 94-98) returns early with plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered from pluginTarget(ctx, pluginCtx.PluginID) without ever invoking the wrapped call m.next / fn, so the actual plugin request is never executed when the plugin is not found in the registry. WHY: a metrics-only concern now gates request execution — any request whose plugin is not resolvable (or whose ID is empty/unknown) is aborted and the caller receives ErrPluginNotRegistered instead of the plugin's real response/error, breaking request semantics for that path. HOW: resolve the target once and fall back to an "unknown" label value (still forward to m.next) instead of returning the lookup error, e.g. capture target via pluginTarget but proceed with fn(ctx) and only skip/annotate the metric when it is unavailable.

issues.descricao: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so logs written via the contextual logger are lost to assertions on the original fake.
issues.textoGolden: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger instead of the receiver. WHY: LoggerMiddleware calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info so the write goes to a throwaway instance and assertions on the original TestLogger Calls/Message never observe it, diverging from real wrapper that preserves logger context. HOW: Return f (or a child sharing f) instead of NewTestLogger.

issues.descricao: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the middleware was renamed to MetricsMiddleware.

comentarios.texto: TestInstrumentationMiddleware still carries the old name even though this PR renamed the middleware under test to MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware/NewMetricsMiddleware) and the file to metrics_middleware_test.go. The identifier advertises the superseded "InstrumentationMiddleware" name; rename it (e.g. TestMetricsMiddleware) so the test name matches the code it exercises.
Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware but it constructs and asserts MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware). Rename to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed middleware.

issues.descricao: The FromContext doc comment is copied from New() and misdescribes the method, which attaches attributes stored in the context.Context.

sugestoes.texto: enableSqlExpressions always returns false: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough `return false`, so the function is a constant and the FlagSqlExpressions check is dead code. WHY: the feature flag is computed but never honored — the flag can never enable SQL expressions regardless of its value (and the negation is logically inverted), so if the intent was to keep the toggle as a kill-switch, it is broken. HOW: return the computed value based on the flag (e.g. `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`) or, if the intent is to fully disable SQL expressions, remove the unused flag computation and the dead branch.

issues.descricao: The variable in TablesList is still named duckDB although it no longer holds a DuckDB instance.

comentarios.texto: After replacing `duck.NewInMemoryDB()` with local `NewInMemoryDB()` and removing the duck import, the local `duckDB` still carries the old implementation name though it is no longer a duck DB. Rename to `db`/`sqlDB` (as done in sql_command.go) so identifier matches code.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches, so ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression query as not implemented even when the sqlExpressions feature flag is enabled.
The variable `enabled` in enableSqlExpressions holds the negated flag value, so it is true when SQL expressions are disabled and the name states the opposite of its value.
NewInMemoryDB returns a stateless stub whose methods all return 'not implemented', so its name misleads callers expecting a working in-memory database.
